description: The plot illustrates how three accuracy-related quantities vary with initial confidence, showing “Final Accuracy” (blue), “Initial Accuracy” (green), and “Δ Accuracy” (orange) with error bars. The x-axis is labeled “Initial Confidence,” appears linear, and spans approximately 0.82 to 0.99 with tick labels at about 0.01 intervals (0.82, 0.83, …, 0.99). The y-axis is labeled “Accuracy,” appears linear, and ranges from about 0.0 up to about 1.2 with regularly spaced ticks (approximately every 0.2). The blue line (solid with circular markers) starts near 1.0 at the leftmost confidence (~0.82), dips slightly just below 1.0 at the next point, then generally increases across the x-axis, reaching roughly 1.18–1.20 by the rightmost confidence (~0.99), with small local fluctuations around the mid-range. The green line (dash-dot with square markers) begins around 0.55–0.60 at ~0.82, rises overall with noticeable step-like increases and small dips (e.g., around the mid-confidence region), and ends near about 1.15–1.18 at ~0.99. The orange line (dashed with diamond markers) starts around 0.45–0.50 at ~0.82, drops to its lowest point near ~0.30 around ~0.86, then increases with oscillations, reaching roughly 0.70–0.75 near the highest confidences (~0.97–0.99); all three series include vertical error bars at each marker indicating variability around the plotted values.
